A multi-task FM that jointly predicts long_view (primary) and is_click (auxiliary) from shared embeddings, combined with 5-seed rank-averaging ensemble, will outscore the single-task FM baseline by at least 0.002 on validation primary
mechanism: is_click is positive 46% of the time vs 33% for long_view, providing denser gradient signal to the shared embeddings. Since P(lv=1|click=0)=0.003, the click head constrains embeddings to capture the engagement signal that nearly determines long_view. With only ~44 train rows per user, the auxiliary task provides extra supervision that stabilises user embeddings. Rank-averaging across 5 seeds then reduces variance of the within-user ordering, which is exactly what the metric measures.

evidence.task_structure: 5.58 impressions/user in validation means small within-user lists where better-calibrated embeddings matter. 98.1% coverage means user embeddings are well-defined. The metric is within-user ordering so any feature constant per user cancels; click provides per-video signal that varies within a user's list.
evidence.previous_experiments: Pooled runs: ensembling 60% accept, median +0.00177. Multi-task auxiliary explicitly flagged as 'largest measured, untried signal' with measured lift table. Task notes say these two compose.

hypothesis: Combining (a) 5-seed FM ensemble with within-user rank averaging and (b) Bayesian-smoothed per-video long_view rate as a bucketed feature will improve validation primary by ~0.002-0.003 over the baseline, clearing the noise floor
mechanism: Rank averaging across seeds reduces the variance of pairwise orderings within each user's ~5-impression list — small score perturbations that flip rankings in one seed are cancelled out across seeds. The smoothed video CTR bucket provides a calibrated prior for how engaging a video is, derived from training history only, adding signal beyond what the video embedding alone captures for videos with sparse training data. Both effects compose because they address different sources of error: variance (ensembling) and bias (CTR prior).

evidence.task_structure: With ~5 impressions per user, a single rank flip changes GAUC and nDCG@5 substantially. Reducing ordering variance via ensembling directly targets the small-list structure. The smoothed CTR adds a continuous quality signal that varies across candidates shown to the same user.
evidence.previous_experiments: Historical runs: ensembling 60% accept rate, median +0.00177, best +0.00237. Smoothed CTR +0.0008 alone. Together measured at +0.0025 in one prior run. Node 0 is the clean baseline parent.

hypothesis: Adding an is_click auxiliary BCE head (weight 0.3) sharing all FM embeddings will improve validation primary by at least 0.002 over node 3 (0.6035), reaching ~0.606+
mechanism: Each training row now carries two supervision signals (long_view + is_click). The click label is better balanced (46% vs 33%) and nearly determines long_view. More gradient signal per row sharpens user/video embeddings, especially for users with few long_view positives. The shared representation learns to separate clickable-and-watched from clickable-but-not-watched.

evidence.task_structure: 44 rows/user in train, 33% LV positive rate means ~15 LV positives per user. With 46% click rate they get ~20 click positives — 33% more supervision. P(lv=1|click=1)=0.9958 means click ranking nearly perfectly recovers LV ranking, so click embeddings directly help the LV task.
